issues.item: Threat: Door and Lock Checking: I repeatedly check that doors and windows are locked
issues.explanation: Door/window checking implies a current intruder or personal safety threat theme that does not fit well with a trauma-to-a-loved-one profile centered on ambulances, anniversaries, and crash imagery. It is weakly connected to the listed triggers and memories, which point more toward accident/reminder-based re-experiencing than home-security threat.

issues.item: Memory: Olfactory Recall: When I think about the frightening event I can sometimes smell things that I smelt when the frightening event happened.
issues.explanation: Olfactory reliving is not impossible, but with the rest of the profile the memory content is underspecified and less clearly tied to the identified trigger-threat pattern. Given the strong formulation emphasis on Triggers ↔ Threat, this item is less coherent than the other memory items unless there was a clear sensory cue from the loved-one trauma scene.

issues.item: Door and Lock Checking: I repeatedly check that doors and windows are locked
issues.explanation: This item is hard to reconcile with the stated trauma type of trauma to a loved one and with the rest of the profile. The triggers and memory items center on accident/emergency reminders, and the threat items otherwise reflect hyperarousal, but repeated door/window checking implies an ongoing home-intrusion or direct personal attack threat context that is not represented elsewhere in the self-report or formulation. With this trauma type, that specific safety behavior is clinically mismatched.
